## Pantoken shadcn/ui Registry — Discovery Report

### Executive Summary

Pantoken operates a **static, schema-conformant shadcn/ui registry** published to `https://pantoken.app/r/` via Cloudflare Workers. The registry is **script-generated** from a canonical component catalog, serves **JSON manifests for direct CLI installation**, and integrates with the CLI via URL delegation to the official shadcn/ui package manager. The registry bridges Instructure design tokens into shadcn's CSS-variable contract and provides pre-built React component implementations.

## I. PUBLISHED REGISTRY STRUCTURE & DISCOVERY

### Publication Details

| Property | Evidence |
|----------|----------|
| **Endpoint** | `https://pantoken.app/r/{name}.json` |
| **Catalog Index** | [`docs/public/r/registry.json`](docs/public/r/registry.json) |
| **Schema Compliance** | Conformant to `https://ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry.json` and `https://ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry-item.json` |
| **Deployment** | Cloudflare Workers / Static asset delivery via CDN |
| **Discovery** | Interactive browser at [/r/](docs/r/index.md) or direct API call to `/r/registry.json` |
| **Item Count** | ~60+ items (themes, components, hooks, base) — see [docs/public/r/](docs/public/r/) directory |

### Item Types Published

Generated from [docs/scripts/generate-registry.ts#L48-L213](docs/scripts/generate-registry.ts#L48-L213):

1. **`registry:theme`** (3 items):

   - `theme-rebrand` — Modern Instructure brand

2. **`registry:base`** (1 item):
   - `base` — Core pantoken system (CSS, components, shadcn bridge)

3. **`registry:ui`** (~50 components):
   - Auto-generated from [formats/components/src/components/index.ts](formats/components/src/components/index.ts) `COMPONENTS` registry
   - Examples: `button`, `alert`, `badge`, `modal`, `tooltip`, `menu`, `pagination`, `table`, `tabs`, etc.

```sh

npx shadcn@latest add https://pantoken.app/r/button.json

# CLI shorthand (delegates via registry URL)
npx pantoken add button

# Multi-item install
npx shadcn@latest add https://pantoken.app/r/theme-canvas.json https://pantoken.app/r/button.json
```

### Implementation Gaps & Best Practices

| Gap | Impact | Mitigation |

| **Direct component exports not in registry** | Can't install `<instui-modal>` web component via registry | Registry is React-only; web components available only via `@pantoken/web-components` package |

## Plugin Audit Complete

I've completed a thorough, read-only discovery of all 18 plugin packages in the pantoken workspace for shadcn `@pantoken` registry suitability. Full detailed findings saved to session memory at `/memories/session/plugin-audit-for-registry.md`.

### **FINDINGS SUMMARY**

**18 Total Plugins:**
- **7 suitable for registry** (CSS components, styles, utilities, themes)
- **5 token-layer/library only** (not registry items)
- **1 private/internal** (deprecations)
- **5 build-tool integrations** (PostCSS, Vite, Webpack, Tailwind, Panda, Next.js)

---

### **✅ RECOMMENDED REGISTRY ITEMS** (7 plugins → 10+ items)

| Plugin | Items | Type | Status |
|--------|-------|------|--------|
| **custom-components** | `@pantoken/card`, `@pantoken/banner`, `@pantoken/agent-shell` | `registry:style` | Sealed; rich cssdoc |

- ✅ Canonical records/exports: All use `definePlugin()` or factory patterns with JSDoc
- ✅ CSS paths: Pre-built `.css` files in `dist/` or generated during build
- ✅ Dependencies: Minimal (mostly `@pantoken/plugin-kit`, `@pantoken/css`, token variables)

### **❌ NOT SUITABLE FOR REGISTRY**

The initial audit identifies the right candidate families, but plugin capability alone is not enough: a registry item needs a published, consumer-loadable artifact and a clear composition contract. I’m verifying each candidate’s exports and naming so the plan excludes token-only or dynamically generated plugins and avoids collisions with core component names.

The manifests confirm five strong plugin families with published CSS, but the audit overcounted layout records and misclassified logos as files when they already ship CSS. I’m narrowing the registry model to what the packages actually export and checking whether aggregate and per-record installation are both available.

The applicable set is now narrower and evidence-based: custom components, layouts, custom icons, logos, custom theme colors, primitives, and visual debug all publish CSS; token transforms and build integrations do not belong in the registry. I’m checking their actual record granularity and configuration semantics before deciding bundle-versus-individual item names.

The source reveals another important distinction: some plugin folders contain docs/page-layout assets that are not exported by the plugin’s CSS hook. Registry generation must follow public exports, not directory discovery, or it will advertise unavailable styles. I’m resolving those export lists and then I’ll fold a precise plugin phase into the plan.

Two corrections matter for implementation: layouts currently publish only an aggregate stylesheet despite exporting seven templates, and Simple Icons does publish both a bundle and per-icon CSS, so it is applicable but should not explode the main registry into thousands of entries. I’m checking built artifact names and plugin metadata hooks to settle bundle and curated-item behavior.

The plugin registry should expose consumer concepts, not package internals: individual custom components and layouts, product-level logo sets, icon collections, theme-color choices, primitives, and visual debug. It should also feed the standalone mockup workflow through the existing plugin CDN manifest, while build-time and token-only plugins stay package-only.

I’m applying that scope to the persisted plan now, including per-layout export work where the current package only offers an aggregate stylesheet and bounded catalog strategies for large icon/logo sets.

The audit also found two plugin consistency gaps that should be fixed as part of registry onboarding: the custom-components runtime hook omits `agent-shell`, and the layouts runtime hook emits only `wrapper` even though the published aggregate contains seven layouts. The plan will gate registry publication on aligning those hooks, generated CSS, exports, and tests.
I’m persisting the final expanded plan with plugin catalog rules, explicit exclusions, standalone CDN discovery, and drift checks.

+# Using the Pantoken registry
+
+The indexed `@pantoken` namespace is a machine-readable CSS catalog for package-managed projects
+that already use the shadcn CLI. Pantoken does not provide React components through this registry.
+Items install Pantoken package dependencies and add CSS imports to the global stylesheet configured
+in `components.json`.
+
+## Discover before installing
+
+```sh
+npx shadcn@latest list @pantoken
+npx shadcn@latest search @pantoken --query modal
+npx shadcn@latest view @pantoken/modal
+npx shadcn@latest add @pantoken/modal
+```
+
+The official registry index resolves `@pantoken` to `https://pantoken.app/r/{name}.json` and adds
+the namespace to `components.json` when needed. `npx pantoken add modal` remains a convenience alias
+for the final command.
+
+Review `view` output before installation. Registry schema validation checks structure, not whether
+the installed CSS or dependency is appropriate for an application.
+
+## Item types
+
+- `base` installs the Pantoken token foundation, base styles, shadcn bridge, and Tailwind v4 aliases.
+- `theme-*` items select Rebrand, Canvas, or Canvas High Contrast token CSS.

+production bundles. Treat primitive utilities as an escape hatch after semantic utilities, and
+remove visual-debug classes before production.

+
+For plain HTML without shadcn, install `@pantoken/components` directly or use the CDN workflow. For

+dedicated Pantoken package or CLI integration. For full React components, use `@instructure/ui-*`;
